answer: Require each agent to earn a scarce, nontransferable reputation by completing randomly assigned tasks whose outcomes are checked against independent evidence. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply trust; each must separately spend time and pass checks before its work can influence payouts. For instance, a marble inventory task might compare walnut counts with a sparrow’s logged delivery. The attacker pays in labor and delay, while coordinated agents risk detection when their supposedly independent results match suspiciously.
